name: Neutrinos from the primary proton–proton fusion process in the Sun

date.note: Exact day within August 2014 not confirmed by a source fetched this session; month precision used.

title: Neutrinos from the primary proton–proton fusion process in the Sun

claim.quote: those from proton–proton fusion have hitherto eluded direct detection. Here we report spectral observations of pp neutrinos, demonstrating that about 99 per cent of the power of the Sun, 3.84 × 1033 ergs per second, is generated by the proton–proton fusion process.

summary.plain: Borexino directly measured, for the first time, the spectrum of the most common neutrinos the Sun makes — the ones from the very first step of the reaction that powers it.
summary.technical: First direct spectral measurement of pp-chain solar neutrinos (the reaction producing ~99% of the Sun's power), made with the Borexino liquid-scintillator detector at LNGS.

why_it_matters.value: Direct spectral observation of the pp neutrinos, which make up nearly the entirety of the solar neutrino flux and had hitherto eluded direct detection, demonstrating that about 99 per cent of the Sun's power is generated by proton-proton fusion.
why_it_matters.quote: These so-called pp neutrinos constitute nearly the entirety of the solar neutrino flux ... Spectral observations of the low-energy neutrinos produced by proton–proton fusion in the Sun demonstrate that about 99 per cent of the Sun’s power is generated by this process.
